analysis: Examined DaemonStateFile.swift base and head. The change adds three optional diagnostic fields to DaemonState: enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery (head lines 54-70, init params 374-378, assignments 413-417). The new fields hold model identifiers and scheduling/blocker strings, and are Optional so older state files still decode. The write/read paths (head lines 658-677) are unchanged. They use best-effort atomic writes to ~/.darkbloom/daemon-state.json. They add no new trust decisions, authorization, attestation or key material. The file remains a local diagnostic that is not authoritative, consistent with existing comments. Model names are already public through heartbeats, so the new fields add no meaningful disclosure. The SelectedModelRecovery.swift added file (unit 81f267b051da25ee:0) has no visible body text here, only a truncated patch excerpt. The excerpt shows a pure in-memory struct with backoff constants, an entry map, a Task handle and enqueue/remove. It does not touch network, crypto or disk. Open questions for integration: (1) the ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery caller was not supplied. It evicts idle unselected models after 120s idle, and eviction interplay with in-flight requests, add-on hold (T-059) and TB-007/T-029 resource availability needs checking there. (2) Whether the blocker string written to the state file can embed sensitive detail (paths, error text) was not visible. The excerpt was truncated, so this is unverified. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
